summary: This small program creates a Thermostat set to 72 degrees and prints the status it reports. It is a hand-check: you run it, read the output, and see for yourself whether the class behaves as expected before writing automated tests.

lines.text: A separate class holds the program's starting point, keeping the runnable app apart from the Thermostat class it exercises.
Java begins execution here, so anything you want to try out by hand goes inside this method.
Creating the object with new calls the Thermostat constructor and passes 72.0 as the current temperature, giving you a concrete instance to question.
Asking the object for its status and printing the result is manual testing: you compare what appears on screen against what you believe should happen at 72 degrees.
